# EV Charging Network Performance & Grid Optimization Report

## Overview

You are tasked with producing an analytical report on EV charging network operations for infrastructure managers and grid planners. The report should transform raw operational data into clear, actionable intelligence that helps leadership make decisions about capacity expansion, load balancing strategies, pricing adjustments, and renewable energy integration.

The audience is management-level — they need data-forward insights but presented with clarity. Lead with KPIs, support with well-chosen visualizations, and close each section with concrete takeaways.

## Key Priorities

- **Queue & Wait Time Analysis is critical.** Customer experience directly ties to wait times, and this is where operational pain points surface most visibly. Give this section strong visual treatment — heatmaps by time slot and location type work well here.
- **The Optimization Recommendations section must be genuinely actionable.** Don't just restate findings — synthesize across all prior sections and propose specific interventions (e.g., load shifting to off-peak windows, pricing incentives during high-renewable periods).
- **Renewable Energy Ratio deserves prominent placement** as a sustainability KPI. Show how it varies by weather condition and time slot to highlight when green charging is most achievable.
- **Segment everything meaningfully.** Location type (Urban/Highway/Suburban) and time slot are the two most important dimensions — make sure they appear consistently across sections so readers can compare patterns.

## Data Integrity

**Do NOT fabricate any numbers, statistics, or trends.** Every figure in the report must be derived directly from `data.csv`. If data is missing or ambiguous, note the limitation rather than inventing values.

## Output Format

Deliver the final report as `/app/output/final_report.html`. Use a clean, professional layout with a dashboard-style feel — embedded charts, a KPI summary banner near the top, and a navigable structure with section anchors. Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and column descriptions.

2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

4	
5	This dataset originates from Kaggle (mjawad17/ev-charging-and-grid-optimization-data) and captures multi-variable interactions within a smart-grid EV charging network. 10	- **Time Range**: Data begins from January 1, 2025 and covers a simulated operational period.
11	
12	## Column Schema
13	
14	| Column Name | Type | Description |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| timestamp | String | Date and time of the record logging (format: M/D/YYYY H:MM) |
17	| station_id | String | Unique identifier for the charging station (e.g., ST004, ST019) |
18	| location_type | String | Categorical location: Urban, Highway, Suburban |
19	| vehicle_id | String | Unique identifier for the electric vehicle (e.g., EV10000) |
20	| vehicle_type | String | Type of EV: Two-Wheeler, Car, Bus, Sedan, SUV, Truck, etc. |
21	| arrival_time | String | Exact time the vehicle arrived at the station |
22	| charging_start_time | String | Time when the active charging session began |
23	| charging_end_time | String | Time when the active charging session finished |
24	| waiting_time | Integer | Time spent in queue before charging started (minutes) |
25	| battery_capacity_kWh | Integer | Total battery capacity of the vehicle (kWh) |
26	| initial_soc | Float | State of Charge (%) when the vehicle arrived |
27	| final_soc | Integer | State of Charge (%) upon session completion |
28	| energy_consumed_kWh | Float | Total energy transferred to the vehicle during the session (kWh) |
29	| charging_power_kW | Integer | Power delivery rate of the assigned charger (kW) |
30	| charging_duration | Float | Total time spent actively charging (minutes) |
31	| queue_length | Integer | Number of vehicles waiting at the station upon arrival |
32	| station_load | Float | Current electrical load on the station's local grid (kW) |
33	| electricity_price | Float | Dynamic cost of electricity during the session (currency units) |
34	| renewable_energy_ratio | Float | Proportion of grid energy from renewable sources (0 to 1) |
35	| traffic_density | String | Local traffic conditions: Low, Medium, High |
36	| weather_condition | String | Weather during the session: Clear, Cloudy, Rainy, Snowy, etc. |
37	| day_of_week | String | Day the session occurred: Monday through Sunday |
38	| time_slot | String | Categorical time block: Peak, Off-Peak, Mid-Peak |
39	| charging_demand | Float | Aggregated demand score for the station at that time |
40	| assigned_charger_id | String | Specific charger unit allocated (e.g., CH1, CH4, CH9) |
41	| charging_priority | String | Priority level: Low, Medium, High |
42	| optimization_reward | Float | Synthetic reward metric for reinforcement learning; can be negative |

45

48	- **optimization_reward** can be negative, representing suboptimal grid conditions or high costs; positive values indicate favorable optimization outcomes.
49	- **renewable_energy_ratio** ranges from 0 to 1, where higher values indicate greater renewable energy penetration.
50	- **electricity_price** varies dynamically and is expected to correlate with time_slot and demand conditions.
51	- The dataset is synthetic/simulated, designed for machine learning and optimization research. Data quality is generally clean with no explicitly documented missing values, but analysts should verify completeness during processing.

53	- **vehicle_type** includes a diverse fleet from Two-Wheelers to Buses, each with different battery capacities and charging profiles.
54	
55	## Analysis Potential
56	
57	The dataset supports multi-dimensional analysis across temporal patterns (day_of_week, time_slot), spatial dimensions (station_id, location_type), vehicle characteristics (vehicle_type, battery_capacity_kWh), environmental factors (weather_condition, traffic_density), and economic variables (electricity_price, renewable_energy_ratio). import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import json

df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# ── KPIs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
kpis = {
    "total_sessions": int(len(df)),
    "avg_waiting_time": round(df['waiting_time'].mean(), 2),
    "avg_energy_consumed": round(df['energy_consumed_kWh'].mean(), 2),
    "mean_station_load": round(df['station_load'].mean(), 2),
    "avg_renewable_ratio": round(df['renewable_energy_ratio'].mean(), 4),
    "mean_opt_reward": round(df['optimization_reward'].mean(), 4),
    "total_energy_kwh": round(df['energy_consumed_kWh'].sum(), 2),
    "unique_stations": df['station_id'].nunique(),
    "unique_vehicles": df['vehicle_id'].nunique(),
}
print("KPIs:", json.dumps(kpis, indent=2))

# ── Location type summaries ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
loc_stats = df.groupby('location_type').agg(
    sessions=('station_id','count'),
    avg_wait=('waiting_time','mean'),
    avg_energy=('energy_consumed_kWh','mean'),
    avg_load=('station_load','mean'),
    avg_renew=('renewable_energy_ratio','mean'),
    avg_reward=('optimization_reward','mean'),
    avg_queue=('queue_length','mean'),
).round(2)
print("\nLocation Type Stats:\n", loc_stats.to_string())

# ── Time slot summaries ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ts_stats = df.groupby('time_slot').agg(
    sessions=('station_id','count'),
    avg_wait=('waiting_time','mean'),
    avg_energy=('energy_consumed_kWh','mean'),
    avg_load=('station_load','mean'),
    avg_renew=('renewable_energy_ratio','mean'),
    avg_reward=('optimization_reward','mean'),
    avg_queue=('queue_length','mean'),
    avg_price=('electricity_price','mean'),
).round(2)
print("\nTime Slot Stats:\n", ts_stats.to_string())

# ── Day of week ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dow_order = ['Monday','Tuesday','Wednesday','Thursday','Friday','Saturday','Sunday']
dow_stats = df.groupby('day_of_week').agg(
    sessions=('station_id','count'),
    avg_wait=('waiting_time','mean'),
    avg_load=('station_load','mean'),
).round(2).reindex(dow_order)
print("\nDay of Week:\n", dow_stats.to_string())

# ── Weather condition ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
wx_stats = df.groupby('weather_condition').agg(
    sessions=('station_id','count'),
    avg_renew=('renewable_energy_ratio','mean'),
    avg_wait=('waiting_time','mean'),
    avg_load=('station_load','mean'),
).round(3)
print("\nWeather Stats:\n", wx_stats.to_string())

EOF

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# ── Station-level stats for bar chart ─────────────────────────────────────────

print("Load ratio (peak/offpeak):", round(
    df[df['time_slot']=='Peak']['station_load'].mean() /
    df[df['time_slot']=='Off-Peak']['station_load'].mean(), 2))

print("\nSessions by time_slot:")
print(df['time_slot'].value_counts())

# ── Sessions with wait > 15 min ───────────────────────────────────────────────
long_wait = (df['waiting_time'] > 15).sum()

print(df['optimization_reward'].describe().round(2))

2. Queue Length & Waiting Time Analysis

Finding

High traffic density correlates with lower wait times (9.43 min) versus Low (9.58 min) and Medium (9.59 min). This suggests traffic volume is not the primary wait-time driver — station capacity and charger allocation matter more.

Tail Risk

Station load is remarkably stable across all days (range: 52.8–53.4 kW mean), suggesting demand is uniformly distributed with no strong weekday vs. weekend differentiation. Load management efforts should focus on intraday time-slot shifts rather than day-of-week scheduling.

4. Renewable Energy Integration & Dynamic Pricing

Vehicles arrive at 34.8% SoC and depart at 98.5% SoC — a near-full charge every session. This deep-charging behavior drives the long average session duration (178 min) and presents an opportunity for smart charging cutoffs at 80–85% to free capacity during peak hours.

6. Optimization Insights & Recommendations

Synthesis Signal

The network's mean optimization reward is −11.83 with only 9.7% of sessions positive. The primary drivers of poor reward are peak-period grid stress (load 2.43× higher than off-peak) and low renewable penetration during peak windows (29% vs. 39% off-peak). The following recommendations address root causes directly.

Priority 1 — Load Shifting

Implement Differentiated Peak Pricing

  • Current pricing shows no meaningful peak/off-peak differential (9.92–9.99). Introduce a 30–50% peak surcharge to incentivize load shifting.
  • Pair with off-peak discounts (−20%) during Off-Peak windows where renewable ratio is highest (39.3%).
  • Target: shift 15–20% of peak sessions to off-peak, reducing peak load from 84 kW toward 70 kW mean.
  • Use charging priority (High/Medium/Low) as the tiering basis for pricing brackets.
Priority 2 — Renewable Maximization

Renewable-Linked Charging Incentives

  • Renewable ratio correlates strongly with optimization reward (r = 0.590) — the clearest single lever for score improvement.
  • Surface real-time renewable ratio to drivers via app; offer green-charging credits when ratio > 35%.
  • Schedule high-power DC fast chargers (50 kW) preferentially during off-peak windows where renewable mix is highest.
  • Target: raise network-wide renewable ratio from 35.4% to 42%+ through demand-side scheduling.
Priority 3 — Queue Management

Smart SoC Cutoff & Slot Reservation

  • All vehicles currently charge to ~98.5% SoC. An 80% smart cutoff option would reduce avg session duration by ~30–40 min, increasing station throughput by an estimated 15–20%.
  • Introduce pre-booking slots for highway stations, which show the highest off-peak queue length (4.70 vehicles).
  • Address the 11.3% of sessions with >15 min wait — target these via dynamic queue re-routing to lower-utilization stations.
Priority 4 — Highway Optimization

Highway Station Efficiency Uplift

  • Highway stations consistently show worse optimization rewards (−12.04 vs Urban −11.63) and higher off-peak queue lengths.
  • Deploy additional fast chargers at highest-load highway stations (ST003: 55.3 kW avg load, ST012: 56.4 kW).
  • Highway traffic patterns are less day-of-week sensitive — implement continuous load monitoring rather than time-of-day scheduling alone.
Priority 5 — Grid Balancing

Reinforcement Learning Reward Improvement
